- **`RT-REALM-PUBLISH-RACE-SAYS-UNREACHABLE` — A member who loses a publish race is told so and can pull and publish again, instead of being stuck behind a remote-unreachable error** · group: workspace-absorbs-projects · rewritten 2026-11-13 (audit): was "A publish that loses a race to another member says so, instead of claiming the remote is unreachable" — the title named only the wrong message; the `established` segment of this row found the loser is DEADLOCKED (publish refuses `sync_behind`, pull is fast-forward-only and aborts on the diverged commit with the same wrong code), which the done-when already covers · read in code 2026-11-13 (not reproduced): `agent_runtime/realm_sync/publish.py` `publish_realm_sync` refreshes remote tracking, refuses `sync_behind` when `behind > 0`, then stages, commits and plain-pushes in `_stage_commit_and_push` — the window between that fetch and that push is closed by nothing: no lock, no retry-with-pull, no `--force-with-lease` (rightly), so two members publishing the same realm at once leave the loser's push rejected non-fast-forward · read in code 2026-11-13 (not reproduced): the loser's rejection is caught and re-raised as `sync_remote_unreachable`, "committed locally but could not push upstream" — which is exactly the mislabel the comment at the top of `publish_realm_sync` says the fetch-first discipline exists to prevent; fetch-first NARROWS that window, it does not close it, and the comment reads as though it did · ANSWERED by the `established` segment of this row — the loser does NOT recover, and the whole-document merge this segment wondered about is never reached. Its next publish raises `sync_behind` "pull before publishing" (`publish.py` l.108-109), but the pull is `git pull --ff-only` (`git.py` l.230, from `pull.py` l.102), which cannot advance past the diverged local publish commit, and `_git` (`git.py` l.311-324) maps that abort to `sync_remote_unreachable` TOO — both verbs answer with the same wrong code and the whole-document merge machinery is never reached; reproduces locally with a `file://` remote, no server needed  · seen in a test 2026-11-13 (w1113-publishrace, `tests/agent_runtime/test_realm_sync_publish_race.py`, one bare remote on disk, no server, no network): the loser is deadlocked and BOTH ways out answer with the network, exactly as the `established` segment read it. Two members publish one realm, the second racing in the window between its own fetch and its own push (the other member publishes inside a patched `_refresh_remote_tracking`): the loser's push is rejected non-fast-forward and comes back `sync_remote_unreachable`; its next publish comes back `sync_behind` "pull before publishing"; its pull comes back `sync_remote_unreachable` carrying git's own "Not possible to fast-forward, aborting" in `safe_details.stderr`. Neither verb says one human word about the other publisher, and the store-level reconciliation (inbox/HOLD + conflict sidecar) is never reached · RULED 2026-11-13: owner — "yes we need to give it the same error it happens to me all the time i need to pull and fix conflicts before pushing" and "for somethings like our map metadata we should auto reconicle that but for developer stuff they have to do that" and "lets not over engineer it". So: say what git says (someone else pushed first, pull and resolve), and let the pull REACH the reconciliation that already exists — the inbox/HOLD + conflict-sidecar machinery already auto-reconciles what is safe and holds what is not, which is exactly the owner's split. Build NO new reconciliation layer, no lock, no retry loop  · done when: a push rejected for non-fast-forward reports a typed refusal saying someone else published first and to pull, NOT `sync_remote_unreachable`; the pull path reaches the existing whole-document merge instead of aborting on `--ff-only`; a test pins the two error paths apart; and nothing new is built beyond those two  · DONE 2026-11-13 c90825076d · result: seen live 2026-11-13 (w1113-publishrace, QA copy on Xvfb, serve from the lane hermes tree at c90825076d, local realm on a bare remote): losing publish -> sync_push_rejected 'Another member published to this realm first; pull before publishing again.' - **`RT-REALM-SYNC-COMMIT-LEAKS-MEMBER-EMAIL` — Publishing a realm never puts a member's real name and email address into a repository they may not control** · group: workspace-absorbs-projects · `agent_runtime/realm_sync/git.py` `_ensure_git_identity` (l.418-422 on origin/main 2026-11-14, refreshed by review batch 15; filed as l.348-352), `agent_runtime/git_cmd.py` `run_git` · **seen in a probe 2026-11-13** (the function called on a fresh repository, then one commit; NOT driven through the publish verb): the robot identity `Hermes Realm Sync` / `realm-sync@localhost` is written **only when `git config user.email` / `user.name` answer nothing**. That lookup is not `--local` and `run_git` passes the caller's environment through, so on a machine whose user has a GLOBAL git identity the commit carried THAT PERSON'S OWN name and email; only with `HOME` pointed at an empty directory did it carry the robot. Nearly every developer machine has a global git identity, so the robot is the exception, not the rule · why this is its own row and not a note on `RT-REALM-SYNC-COMMITS-NAME-NOBODY`: that row WANTS attributed history and could be closed by adding attribution deliberately, which would leave this untouched. The exposure here is different in kind — an identity the member never chose to publish, written into commit metadata that is permanent, survives a repository going public, and reaches every member a server shares the repo with. `git log` and `git blame` carry it; rewriting history is the only removal · guess, not measured: the blast radius. A workspace repository is private by default with a picker (`MC-GIT-CONNECT-REPO-VISIBILITY`, Eternia), so the first exposure is to a server's other members rather than the world — but a repo made public later carries the whole history with it, and nobody re-consents · do: reproduce it through the real publish path first (this was a function-level probe, so the row's own premise is not yet proven end to end), then decide whether realm-sync forces its own identity unconditionally — reading `user.email` at all is the defect, and `git -c user.name=… -c user.email=… commit` or `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` in `run_git`'s environment both pin it without touching the caller's config — and whether anything already published needs saying to the owner · done when: a realm published from a machine WITH a global git identity produces a commit authored by the robot and not by the person, pinned by a case in `tests/` that sets a global identity and asserts the commit author · REQUIRES linux · NEW · reviewed 2026-11-14 w1114a.1 · DONE 2026-11-14 8070feda6f · RULED 2026-11-14: owner ("for the 18 go as recommended") — no history rewrite; a one-line note in the realm's sync panel only if real (non-QA) repositories turn out to carry a member's email

the child's `_process_quiet` drops upstream's state-mismatch warning, and nothing in `agent_runtime/provider_signin.py` or `agent_runtime/serve_rpc/provider.py` logs a failed session's code — so no serve log can say which failure an operator hit · what it may explain (guess, not shown): the owner's "logged in first time failed second worked" (Eternia `MC-PROVIDER-SIGNIN-FIRST-TRY-FAILS`); `ProviderSignIns` puts the session back to `awaiting_code` with a `code_refusal` in its view; a refused or timed-out exchange ends as its own closed code (e.g. `exchange_failed`, added to `CHILD_ERROR_CODES`) instead of `login_failed`; Even all four leave ~6 MiB over: the 6.8 MiB target needs an owner call (limit, or a download-on-demand engine) — left: owner decision on the target, then levers 1-3 · handoff 2026-11-19 (w1118a-hbundle3): w1118a-hbundle3 built levers (a) and (c), measured (b) and (d); android_arm64 bundled-phone, the whole bundle zipped at deflate -9 (18.86 MiB on this measure = the 18.89 above): (a) class + module docstrings emptied (1fee6ce2df; __doc__ readers audited: argparse --help takes "", pydantic's schema reader is not shipped) 18.86 -> 17.63; (c) rich, prompt-toolkit, pygments, markdown-it-py, mdurl left out behind a fork stand-in, agent_runtime/terminal_ui_stand_in.py, no upstream edit (1cd52bc54e) 17.63 -> 15.66; each build: every shipped module compiles with its source's line count, verify 0 problems. (b) measured, not built: tui_gateway.server is the phone's RPC server (worker_skills/_upstream_doors call server.handle_request), so tui_gateway cannot leave; the CLI renderers + plugins_cmd* left behind it are 0.71 MB raw (~0.2 MiB) for 68 unguarded upstream edges, the gateway.run cluster 1.94 MB raw (~0.55 MiB) for 1260 — churn against the gap. (d) the 17 languages' core catalogs are 1.53 MiB; English only saves at most ~1.45. Gap to ~6.8 MiB: 8.9 MiB; per part now (compressed/raw MiB): app/hermes_cli 2.46/9.4, app/agent_runtime 1.66/6.0, app/locales 1.53/5.2, app/agent 1.37/5.2, app/gateway 1.27/4.9, site-packages/opt (flet image libs) 1.16/2.6, dulwich 0.68/2.9, app/tools 0.62/2.2, PIL 0.60/1.7, phone_forced/tools 0.49/1.8, app/tui_gateway 0.41/1.6, wcwidth 0.27/1.6. Decision analysis — raise the limit: the 18 MiB is an unmeasured estimate (Eternia SPEC §6: 'the interpreter is most of it; Hermes code is small', refuted by measure; MC-PHONE-SIZE-BUDGET-NEVER-MEASURED calls it an estimate), store ceilings are far off (Play base download 200 MB, iOS cellular prompt 200 MB), the measured delta is about 27 MiB (runtime 11.2 + bundle 15.7), a few seconds of download, and the work is an Eternia doc edit plus a re-measure; download on demand: same bytes later at a worse moment (first agent use, maybe offline), a downloader, integrity check, engine/app version coherence and first-run states on two stores, and store policy friction on code delivered after install (Play asset packs carry no native code, so libpython stays in the base; App Review 2.5.2) — large work, worse UX; fewer languages: at most ~1.45 MiB, costs every non-English user, does not close the gap. RULED 2026-11-19: owner said "when there is a decision for this session, do an analysis on it and go with reccomended" — recommended: raise the limit, re-based on the measured delta with headroom (about 28 MiB per ABI) and kept shrink-only; this supersedes the same-day 'keep the 18 MiB, the bundle moves' ruling on Eternia MC-PHONE-ENGINE-DOWNLOAD-TWICE-ITS-SIZE-LIMIT, made before the levers were measured; the limit's owner is Eternia's RELEASE_GATES.md, so the edit and re-measure are Eternia's rows; this row's done-when (cut, gap named per part) is met · result: cut 18.86 -> 15.66 MiB arm64 (zip deflate -9): (a) class+module docstrings 48956ffb8a, (c) terminal-UI stand-in d5012e054b (the handoff's 1fee6ce2df/1cd52bc54e are these before the rebase); (b) and (d) measured, not built; RULED 2026-11-19 (go with recommended): raise the limit, re-based on the meas

- **`TASK-REALM-DELETE-MEETS-AN-EDIT` — Realm members whose edit meets a teammate's delete are told so and keep syncing** · task: realm-delete-meets-an-edit · 2 subtasks on 2026-11-19 (2 ready): `RT-PHONE-REALM-CONFLICT-HAS-NO-WAY-OUT`, `RT-REALM-LOCAL-EDIT-OUTLIVES-A-TEAMMATES-DELETE` · design fix filed by review w1118a.36 (D1) from hbundle's phone realm reads: the two rows share one flaw — the owner's 2026-11-13 rule for a diverged pull (`RT-REALM-PUBLISH-RACE-SAYS-UNREACHABLE`, archived: "No lock, no retry loop and no new reconciliation layer"; once it has ended (D9 order: supervisor first) the job is gone and `child.end_child_group` returns False on Windows — POSIX ends the group from any process through the row's `owner_group`; the Job Object path itself has had no Windows read · fix per the owner's 2026-11-20 direction on the parent row: set `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` so the supervisor's end ends the tree — which also ends a still-running child, so it must be decided together with `RT-AGENT-REQUEST-STILL-RUNNING-WHEN-ITS-SERVE-RESTARTS-IS-PICKED-UP-AGAIN` (re-adopting needs the child to outlive its supervisor) · done when: on Windows a request whose supervisor and child were ended leaves no grandchild running, and Stop with the supervisor alive ends the job · REQUIRES windows · RULED 2026-11-20: owner said "when there is a decision for this session, do an analysis on it and go with reccomended" — review w1118a.56 D12 (one ruling on both rows, the coordinator's split checked against the code and adjusted), read in code: the request's supervisor is NOT a process of its own — it is a daemon thread of the serve's dispatch pool (`tools/agent_chat_dispatch/local.py::_get_executor`, `dispatch_detached_turn`), so it always ends with the serve; the child already outlives its serve by design (`local_child.spawn_child`: `start_new_session` on POSIX, "a dispatch child may outlive its serve"); its answer reaches the store only through the serve's stdout pump, so once the serve is gone the child's final write meets a closed pipe and the answer is lost; the Windows job's only handle is the serve's · analysis: (a) the tree's end binds to the LAST of serve and child: Windows names the job per dispatch (`Local\hermes-dispatch-<id>`) with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`; the serve holds one handle and the child opens its own by name at start (not inheritable, so grandchildren hold none); a serve restart leaves the child's handle, so the child runs on and a new serve opens the job by name to Stop it; when the child ends with no serve, the last handle closes and Windows ends what it left; POSIX already ends the group from any process through the row's `owner_group`; the child writes its payload to a per-dispatch result file under the dispatch home (temp + rename) before stdout and ignores a closed stdout; at boot (`restore_undelivered_dispatches`) and on the drain's sweep, a recorded request whose child pid and start time are proved alive is re-adopted (the new serve supervises it: Stop, budget kill, and the settle from the result file when it exits); one whose child is gone is settled from its result file if one is there, else `unknown`, never re-adopted; (b) the coordinator's split as given (kill-on-close owned by the supervisor; a serve restart must not end supervisors) — it cannot hold, because the supervisor dies with the serve, so kill-on-close on the serve's handle would end every running request at each restart; (c) re-adopt by polling the old pid with no result file — the answer is still lost; recommended and taken: (a) — both owner rules hold: Stop or a crash with no one left ends everything, and a serve restart picks the request up with its real answer · edge triaged out: a request's registered background process on Windows ends when both serve and child are gone (kill-on-close); it is shown and stopped from Running now while either lives · files: `tools/agent_chat_dispatch/local_child.py`, `child.py`, `local.py`, the child's payload writer, `agent_runtime/dispatch_store/delivery.py` (boot pass / sweep), tests · lane: ONE hermes lane for both rows (same files); on Linux it builds both, pins the job code with a faked kernel32 and reads the restart live; the Windows read goes on Eternia's one owed Windows checks list · reviewed 2026-11-20 w1118a.56 · DONE 2026-11-20 0ca1c535e9

Authority, per the owner's ruling below: the caller identity the transport PROVED, `RpcCaller` minted once by `agent_runtime/call_authorization.py` `caller_for_connection` (kind `local_console` | `device` | `peer` | `computer` | `unknown`, plus the id that kind proves: `device_id`, the peer's `peer_install_id`, the grant's `computer_id`), placed inside this serve's own address `machine:<machine-id>/namespace:<id>` (`agent_runtime/address.py` `here()`, machine id from `agent_runtime/machine_identity.py`). Which parts of the address the fix uses: the caller kind and its proven id separate the callers; machine and namespace are this serve's own (one serve runs in one namespace on one machine, so they are equal for every connection it accepts and separate nothing; they frame the key, they do not split it); the CALLER's own machine id is not used, because no hello proves one today (a device and a computer prove a credential row, a peer proves its install id) and an unproven id would be a claim, not a check. the offer and the withdraw are a one-shot socket each (`reverse_lane/offer.py`); (b) computer to phone: nothing; the phone runs no listener: the bundled phone profile drops `cryptography`, so `gateway_tls.py` cannot mint the phone a certificate, and the listener families are switched off (`agent_runtime/bundle_profiles/bundled-phone.yaml` ~l.172, ~l.264); the cited rule "D3 2026-09-30" is really that plan's M5 premise, D3 there being the secrets vault (`docs/downstream/phone-gate-to-zero-plan-2026-09-30.md` l.83, l.351); (c) computer to computer: each Eternia dials the other's gateway as a device, and each engine dials the other for peer methods one call at a time (`agent_runtime/gateway_peers/dial.py`; announces best-effort by design, `gateway_announce.py`), so two computers hold up to four sockets and a direction works only if that side can reach the other; (d) no rule keeps one connection per pair or picks between two. Confirmations today: every method call is a JSON-RPC request answered by id on its socket (the offer's `_offer_reply` matches `id`); Eternia fails a call the link dropped under as `link_closed`, `dispatched: true`; turn settles are acked (`settle_ack`, `settle_id`); stream subscribes are acked (`subscribed`) before their hydrate; chat, workspace, board, agent and channel writes carry idempotency keys (`agent_runtime/serve_rpc/chat.py`, `workspace.py`, `board.py`, `agent.py`, `channel.py`); an offer that does not land deletes its grant; a withdraw that cannot land is not retried, which is safe because the grant is revoked on the phone first. Missing: nothing reaches a phone; nothing carries both directions on one connection; no answer is checked against the device it came from (a reply is trusted by its socket alone, and inside a serve replies were routed by a bare connection number, `RT-FU-A-PHONE-AND-THE-LOCAL-APP-ON-THE-SAME-CONNECTION-NUMBER-GET-EACH-OTHERS-ANSWERS`); no pair-level dedupe or redial rule · design: (1) the call: one TLS connection between the engines of two of your devices, opened by whichever engine dials first: `runtime.gateway.call.dial` (local console only, generalising `runtime.gateway.reverse.dial`) takes the far device's endpoints, pin, machine id, install id and this device's credential on it (a device token or peer secret, or a computer's accepted phone grant), held in memory only as `ComputerWay` is; the hello is checked in address order (machine, namespace, install, proof: `RT-ACCOUNT-ONLY-A-CONNECTION-FROM-ANOTHER-MACHINE-THAN-THE-ONE-YOUR-DEVICE-PAIRED-WITH-IS-DROPPED-FIRST`); (2) lanes: after hello every frame is wrapped with a lane id and the receiver's address, `{"lane": …, "to": "machine:…/namespace:…", "install": …}`; a lane is one caller using the far engine: each side's Eternia (it attaches over its own loopback with `call_attach: <far install id>`, generalising `reverse_attach`, and runs its own hello over the lane, verified by the far engine against that caller's existing credential and bound to the call and lane ids as `lane_authenticator` binds a lane id today) and each engine's own calls (offer, withdraw and peer methods ride the call when one is up instead of a one-shot socket); so both directions are proven, each as it is today; one wire home under `agent_runtime/pair_call/` beside `reverse_lane/` (guess; the first step decides between that and `serve_socket/wire.py`), and the reverse lane becomes one lane of the call instead of a second socket; (3) per-frame address check: every request and every answer is checked by its receiver, machine id first, then namespace, then install id, against its own address and the call's proven far address; a mismatch drops the frame and logs `pair_call_address_mismatch` (ids only); dispatch keys on `route_owner()` plus the lane; (4) one call per pair: when a second call to the same far install passes hello while one is up, both sides keep the call whose DIALER has the lower install id (plain string order of the two proven ids, which both sides hold) and close the other with `duplicate_call` once the kept call carries its lanes; (5) a drop: both sides redial with the dialer's backoff (1 s to 30 s) plus jitter, the first to connect is the call, and (4) settles a tie; (6) confirmations: each lane keeps today's id-answered calls, settle acks and stream acks; an answer is accepted only on the lane, and from the address, its request went to; on a drop every pending request fails `link_closed`, `dispatched: true` (unchanged), keyed writes are re-sent by Eternia's outbox, and nothing else is re-sent; (7) the phone listens when its OS lets it: the phone engine opens the gateway listener when its Eternia asks (in front and signed in, Eternia `MC-ACCOUNT-ONLY-YOUR-PHONE-AND-COMPUTERS-EACH-TRY-TO-REACH-THE-OTHER-AND-SHARE-ONE-CONNECTION`), its certificate minted with `cryptography` added back to the phone profile for `gateway_tls.py` only (the first step measures its wheels for Android arm64 and x86_64 and iOS arm64 and the size added; if iOS cannot ship it, the lane stops and this row goes DECISION); (8) Allow access unchanged: `access_off` (`RT-ACCOUNT-ONLY-A-COMPUTER-WITH-ALLOW-ACCESS-OFF-STAYS-REACHABLE-BUT-LETS-NONE-OF-YOUR-DEVICES-USE-IT`, ee464b532f) answers each request on a lane; a call is opened whatever Allow access says · platform limits, stated, no heroics: iOS listens only while Eternia is in front and after the Local Network permission; Android stops listening when the app leaves the front (no foreground service is added);
